transcript.answer: At most three upkeep runs can start per repository for one event, such as a push to main. The pull requests that go first are the ones upkept longest ago. Order: first any pull request that was never upkept, then the one whose newest upkeep run started earliest, then the oldest pull request. Before 2026-10-25 the three oldest pull requests were always picked. The same three failing PRs then took every start and starved the rest. The remaining PRs are left for the next event.

judgements.reason: The answer states the limit of 3 per event per repository and the exact ordering (never upkept, then earliest newest upkeep run, then oldest); the extra history detail does not contradict the gold.
